titleStmt.title: Telegram From the White House Situation Room to President Johnson at the LBJ Ranch, in Texas

div.head: 217. Telegram From the White House Situation Room to President Johnson at the LBJ Ranch, in Texas
div.p: CAP 661063. For the President from Secretary Rusk.

list.item: As you know, Chiang Kai-shek has formally told us that he would withdraw immediately from the UN if the Italian draft study committee resolution passed. The vote on this may come as early as Monday night, so that any further action we take must be done at once.

We gave Ambassador McConaughy all the arguments, and he has laid them out brilliantly to the Gimo, but without apparently budging him. McConaughy has also been hitting every senior Chinese official he can reach. Finally, I have enlisted Walter Judd to write a personal message to the Gimo. However, it seems to me clear that the matter requires a personal message by you, in view of the disastrous effect of such a withdrawal and the very important impact that your personal intervention might have.

I have therefore drafted a fairly short and fundamental letter for your approval. It stresses particularly holding off on any action until I
can visit Taipei on my forthcoming trip, probably between December 5 and December 7 (well after the UN vote).

At same time, I have prepared a longer message from myself to the Chinese Foreign Minister in New York. It is designed to supplement your letter by repeating the more technical arguments. If, however, upon seeing the two messages together, you thought it desirable to transfer some or all of the arguments in the second draft letter to your own letter, this could readily be done.

I hope that you can give me your reaction so as to permit dispatch of both letters as soon as possible. This would permit the Gimo to reflect before his final decision—which as of now appears to be for withdrawal.

note.p: Source: Johnson Library, National Security File, Country File, China, Vol. VII. Secret.

A note from Bromley Smith to Rostow, attached to the source text, states that the President cleared the short version of the letter to Chiang and that the Rusk message to the Foreign Minister was also sent.
